findings.title: Uniform flex-shrink can truncate short segments first
findings.problem: The rule `#identity-bar > span:not(#identity-version-badge) { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }` applies the same default flex-shrink (1) and no per-segment max-width to all six text spans (auth-status, product, account, profile, model, project). With min-width:0 in place, the browser scales all six boxes down by roughly the same proportion of their own content width as the bar narrows.
findings.impact: Because the reduction is proportional rather than priority-weighted, the short, bold auth-status text (the first and most prominent segment) can be ellipsized down to a few characters at the same narrow widths where a lower-priority segment like project still has visible slack. Before this change the bar simply wrapped and nothing was cut, so this inconsistent, avoidable-looking truncation is newly introduced by this diff.
findings.recommendation: Give the shorter, higher-value segments (auth-status, product) a smaller flex-shrink or a floor max-width relative to the longer/optional ones (account, project) so they are not the first to lose readable text. No spec/story exists for this ticket, so the exact priority order is a design call the fix should confirm rather than assume.
